items.definition:
strive to gain or win something by defeating or establishing superiority over others
Athletes compete for gold medals.

be composed or made up of
The team consists of five members.

give (something, especially money or time) in order to help achieve or provide something
Everyone should contribute to the project.

notice or perceive (something) and register it as being significant
Scientists observe the stars.

throw back (heat, light, or sound) without absorbing it
The mirror reflects your image.

refuse to accept
They decided to reject the offer.

to become or make larger or more extensive
The company plans to expand its business.

steal from
Someone tried to rob the bank last night.

make someone admire
He tried to impress his boss with his hard work.

put money into financial schemes, shares, or property with the expectation of achieving a profit
It's wise to invest in your future.

to present something for consideration or approval
Please submit your application by Friday.

to draw attention or interest
The bright colors attract butterflies.

to be brave enough to do something
I dare you to jump into the cold water.

to give out or spread around
Please distribute these flyers to everyone.

to prepare for publication by correcting, revising, or adapting
I need to edit my essay before submitting it.

to travel through an unfamiliar area to learn about it; to examine thoroughly
Let's explore the old castle.

to carry out a systematic or formal inquiry to discover and examine the facts of (an incident, allegation, etc.) so as to establish the truth
The police will investigate the cause of the accident.

to pull something along the ground
He had to drag the heavy box across the floor.

to teach or train someone
Parents have a responsibility to educate their children.

to make something smooth and shiny by rubbing
She used a cloth to polish the silver.

to return to a normal state of health, mind, or strength
It took him a long time to recover from the illness.

to depend on with full trust or confidence
You can always rely on him for help.

to please someone by giving them what they want or need
The meal was enough to satisfy my hunger.

to become aware of something
I didn't realise how late it was.

to go somewhere with someone as a companion or escort
She agreed to accompany him to the party.

to stop feeling angry or resentful towards someone for an offense
Please forgive me for my mistake.

to differ
Prices may vary depending on the season.

to ask for divine favor; to make holy
May God bless you and your family.

to become sound or healthy again
It will take time for the wound to heal.

show, prove
The teacher will demonstrate how to solve the problem.

to break suddenly with a sharp sound; to take a quick photograph
The twig snapped under his foot.

to act dishonestly or unfairly in order to gain an advantage
It's wrong to cheat on an exam.

to order or allow to leave; to treat as unworthy of serious consideration
The teacher dismissed the class early.

to turn over or cause to turn over with a sudden quick movement
He flipped the coin to decide who would go first.

to oppose or fight against
It's hard to resist chocolate.

to offer suggestions about the best course of action
I advise you to study hard for the exam.

to make something cold
Chill the wine before serving.

inspect closely
The doctor will examine your throat.

continue, go forward
Please proceed with your presentation.

to scatter liquid in fine drops
He used a bottle to spray water on the plants.

to adjust to new conditions
It takes time to adapt to a new culture.

to press or squeeze something so hard that it is flattened or broken
He accidentally crushed the empty can.

to make or become smaller or fewer
The number of visitors has decreased.

to create or design something that has not existed before
Thomas Edison invented the light bulb.

to respond
How did he react to the news?

to mark or damage a surface with a sharp object
Be careful not to scratch the new car.

to break open or apart suddenly and violently
The balloon burst when it hit the sharp branch.

to cause (someone) to feel awkward, self-conscious, or ashamed
His rude comments embarrassed everyone at the party.

to deal with; to confront
We need to tackle this problem immediately.

to eat dinner
We decided to dine at a new restaurant tonight.

to incline or bend from a vertical position
Don't lean on the wet paint.

revise
She needs to revise her essay before submitting it.

stare
It's rude to stare at people.

to owe
I owe you five dollars for the coffee.

to conduct the policy, actions, and affairs of (a state, organization, or people)
The new laws will govern how businesses operate.

to say or estimate that a specified thing will happen in the future or will be a consequence of something
It's difficult to predict the weather accurately for next week.

to alter or move something slightly in order to achieve the desired fit, appearance, or result
You can adjust the height of the chair.

to provide amusement or enjoyment
The clown entertained the children with his tricks.

to try to persuade strongly
I urge you to reconsider your decision.

determine (the amount or number of something) mathematically
Can you calculate the total cost for me?

to present or constitute (a problem, danger, etc.)
The new policy could pose a risk to small businesses.

to please greatly
The news delighted everyone.

to make a hole with a drill; to practice
We need to drill a hole in the wall.

to escape or allow to escape through a hole
The pipe started to leak.
